mapping-data-flows.title: Mapping data flows – Azure Data Factory – Microsoft Learn
mapping-data-flows.notes: Mapping data flows are visually designed data transformations in Azure Data Factory; the page states that it also applies to Azure Synapse Analytics. They let developers build transformation logic without writing code, while the service takes care of code translation, path optimization and execution of the data flow jobs on scaled-out Apache Spark clusters. A data flow runs as an activity inside a pipeline, where the integration runtime and parameter values are chosen, so it can use the existing scheduling, control flow and monitoring features. The authoring canvas has a top bar for saving, validating and viewing the JSON or script, a graph that shows the stream from source to sink, and a configuration panel for the selected transformation. Each transformation offers tabs for its own settings, partition optimization, a read-only metadata inspection and a data preview. The data preview works only when debug mode is switched on, and the inspect tab shows no metadata when the source has no defined schema, which is typical for schema drift. The page also points to Dataflow Gen2 in Microsoft Fabric as a comparable technology.

microsoft-365-lighthouse.title: Overview of Microsoft 365 Lighthouse – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-365-lighthouse.notes: Microsoft 365 Lighthouse is a portal that lets managed service providers manage Microsoft 365 customer tenants and deliver their services at scale. Its stated aims are to standardize configurations, manage risk and surface AI-supported sales opportunities. Service engineers can onboard tenants with recommended security configurations for small and medium-sized businesses, work with cross-tenant views, and detect and act on risks. Account managers receive AI-based insights for winning and retaining customers and for adding premium offerings. Described capabilities include tenant deployment workflows, a default security baseline, device compliance insights across tenants, MFA and self-service password reset setup, detection of risky sign-ins, and threat details from Microsoft Defender XDR for Windows 10 devices. The portal also shows service incidents and advisories that affect the managed tenants. Managing Microsoft 365 services and connected devices through it carries no additional cost. It is available to Cloud Solution Provider partners, both direct-bill and indirect resellers, and both the provider and the customer tenants must meet separately listed requirements. Azure Lighthouse is a different offering for Azure services.

microsoft-365-local.title: Microsoft 365 Local Overview – Azure Local – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-365-local.notes: Microsoft 365 Local runs Exchange Server, SharePoint Server and Skype for Business Server on Azure Local infrastructure that the customer owns and manages. Its purpose is to support sovereignty requirements through more control over data residency, access and compliance. It can also modernize existing on-premises deployments of these servers into a sovereign private cloud, and serve as a fallback or business continuity environment that can keep running locally in a crisis. The page describes a validated reference architecture covering networking, storage, compute and identity integration, plus Azure-consistent management with a unified control plane. Two operating modes exist: a connected mode, where Azure acts as a cloud-based control plane for monitoring, updates and policy, and a fully disconnected mode with a local control plane. It must be deployed on an Azure Local Premier Solution from a hardware partner that meets the stated requirements, and deployment goes through a Microsoft-certified Microsoft 365 Local partner in phases such as assessment, planning, acquisition and deployment. The sizing is customer specific and has to be worked out with a Microsoft partner. The page gives no licensing details or pricing.

microsoft-entra-id-p2.title: Microsoft Entra licensing – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-entra-id-p2.notes: Microsoft Entra ID P2 is a license tier of Microsoft Entra ID that is sold on its own and is also included in several bundles. It contains all the listed authentication features of P1 and adds risk-based Conditional Access, which is available only in P2. Identity Protection requires a P2 license and covers risk-based sign-in and user-risk policies enforced through Conditional Access, reports on risky users, risky sign-ins and risk detections, and notifications for users at risk. P2 also includes Privileged Identity Management, including PIM for groups, which needs P2 or Entra ID Governance for every user with eligible or time-bound assignments, for approvers and for access review participants. Further capabilities in the tables are risk-based identity verification, access reviews and entitlement management with access packages. The tier is included in Microsoft 365 E5 and E7, the Defender suites, Enterprise Mobility + Security E5 and the Defender and Purview suites for Business Premium. If a license expires, PIM features stop working and eligible role assignments are removed, while permanent assignments stay. Lifecycle Workflows and some access review features are not part of P2, and workload identities are licensed separately.

microsoft-hololens.title: HoloLens 2 hardware – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-hololens.notes: HoloLens 2 is an untethered holographic computer that continues the first-generation HoloLens and runs the Windows Holographic operating system, a variant of Windows 10. The headset has a flip-up visor holding the sensors and see-through holographic lenses, a headband with an adjustment wheel, and buttons for brightness, volume and power plus a USB-C port. Its sensor set includes cameras for head tracking, infrared cameras for eye tracking, a time-of-flight depth sensor, an inertial measurement unit and an 8-megapixel camera. It runs on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 850 chip with a second-generation holographic processing unit. Interaction works through fully articulated two-handed tracking, real-time eye tracking and voice commands, and the device builds a live mesh of the surroundings. Preinstalled software includes Dynamics 365 Guides for learning new skills and Dynamics 365 Remote Assist for working with remote experts through Teams. Active battery life is stated as two to three hours. A user account is required, the page says the device is not intended for children under 13, and the eye protection only meets basic impact ratings. Natural-language voice input through Cortana needs an internet connection.

microsoft-partner-incentives.title: Getting started – incentives – Partner Center – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-partner-incentives.notes: Partners in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program can take part in incentive programs that reward them for delivering services to customers and are meant to help them grow their business. The page works as an entry point rather than a catalog, and it does not list specific programs, payout amounts or eligibility criteria. The suggested path is to review the available programs under Microsoft investments and incentives, enroll in a program, and check eligibility where the program requires it. Partners then set up payout and tax profiles in Partner Center, which hold the bank and tax details Microsoft needs to make payments. They can also review Microsoft Commerce Incentives engagements and their own eligibility status. Membership in the partner program is required, and the user needs the Incentives admin or Incentives user role. Program details, payout profile and eligibility information must be in place before a payout can happen. The eligibility check applies only to some programs, and further detail sits in linked articles on enrollment, eligibility, profiles and engagements.

microsoft-trust-center.title: Microsoft Trust Center Overview
microsoft-trust-center.notes: The Microsoft Trust Center Overview page presents Microsoft products and services in terms of security, privacy, compliance and transparency, with a short statement that data is handled securely and in line with privacy and legal requirements. It is organized around product tabs for Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, Power Platform and additional products and services. Example entries include Azure AI, Azure OpenAI Service, Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Power Apps and Power BI. For each product the page links to topics such as security, privacy, GDPR, data location and compliance, and Azure AI adds responsible AI, transparency note and limited access. The wider navigation covers data management, data access, data location, regulations such as DORA, the EU AI Act and NIS2, the Secure Future Initiative, Zero Trust, audit reports and Compliance Score. In practice it serves as a starting point: choose a product, then follow the links to the detailed security, privacy and compliance documents. The page itself names no licenses or prerequisites and contains no concrete certifications or audit results, because those details sit on the linked pages.

multi-agent-architecture.title: AI Agent Orchestration Patterns – Azure Architecture Center – Microsoft Learn
multi-agent-architecture.notes: Multi-agent orchestration coordinates several specialized AI agents so they can work together on complex tasks. An orchestrator or a peer-based protocol handles task distribution, context passing and result aggregation. The page credits this design with specialization, easier scaling, simpler testing and the freedom to give each agent its own model, knowledge sources and tools. It describes five patterns: sequential, concurrent, group chat, handoff and magentic, which differ in how work is routed and whether a manager adapts a task list on the fly. The guidance advises choosing the lowest complexity that works, moving from a direct model call to a single agent with tools and only then to several agents, for example when prompt complexity, tool overload or security boundaries make a single agent unreliable. Costs and risks named include coordination overhead, added latency, multiplied model calls, growing context windows, error propagation and endless loops in group chat or handoff. Because agent output is nondeterministic, tests should use rubrics or an LLM judge rather than exact comparison, and observability, authentication and guardrails are expected. Microsoft Agent Framework and Semantic Kernel are named as code-level options.

nonconformance.title: Quality and nonconformance management overview – Supply Chain Management – Microsoft Learn
nonconformance.notes: In Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management, a nonconformance describes an item that has a quality problem. The process creates a nonconformance order that records the quantity of nonconforming material, the source of the problem, the problem type and explanatory notes. Six standard types exist: customer, service request, vendor, production, internal and co-product production, each needing its own source information such as a sales order, purchase order or production order. A new record starts with the status New and can be approved, refused, closed or reopened. Tags and reports carry the nonconformance number, the item and the problem type, and the tag can also show a quarantine zone and a disposition such as unusable or restricted usage. Approved records can carry operations with costs, and a quality order can be created from a nonconformance. A corrections page tracks required fixes with an owner, a due date and a completion status. The stated goals are quick handling regardless of origin, linking diagnostic findings to corrective tasks to avoid repeats, and analysis by problem type. The calculated costs are reference data used only within quality management, and the feature has to be enabled first.

onedrive-files-on-demand.title: Save disk space with OneDrive Files On-Demand for Windows – Microsoft Support
onedrive-files-on-demand.notes: Files On-Demand gives access to every file in OneDrive cloud storage without downloading it and without using local disk space. The page says the feature is on by default from a specific OneDrive build onward. In File Explorer, a blue cloud marks an online-only file that is fetched when opened and cannot be opened offline. A green check marks a locally available file that was opened and downloaded, and a green circle with a white check marks a file set to always stay on the device. Right-click commands let users keep items on the device or free up space, and Storage Sense can return unused files to online-only status after a chosen period. New files appear as online-only by default, except inside a folder marked to always keep files. Desktop search finds online-only files only by name, not by content. The feature needs a supported Windows 10 or Windows Server version, a signed-in OneDrive account and works with OneDrive, SharePoint in Microsoft 365 and SharePoint Server 2019 team sites. It is not supported when Windows Information Protection is enabled, and some third-party antivirus products are incompatible. Deleting an online-only file removes it from OneDrive on all devices, though the recycle bin can restore it.

onedrive-shortcuts.title: Add shortcuts to shared folders in OneDrive – Microsoft Support
onedrive-shortcuts.notes: A shortcut in OneDrive is a link that places a shared folder in the My files area, using the Add shortcut to My files command. Its purpose is to make shared folders easier to reach and edit, including on a PC or Mac where the OneDrive app syncs them. The command is available from the Shared view by selecting a folder and using the circle on its tile or the right-click menu. A shortcut can be renamed, and the new name is visible only to the person who set it. Removing a shortcut deletes just the link, so the folder stays with its owner. The shortcut uses no storage of its own, since the content counts against the owner. Users need to be signed in with a Microsoft account and need edit rights on the shared folder. Only folders are supported, not single shared files. The page states limits of 100 folder shortcuts per person and 1,000 shortcuts overall for files and folders. If the owner stops sharing the folder, it disappears from OneDrive, and removing a shortcut also removes it from synced computers.

onelake-security.title: OneLake security roles, permissions, and scopes – Microsoft Fabric – Microsoft Learn
onelake-security.notes: OneLake security is a role-based access control model for data stored in OneLake. Administrators define security roles that grant access to specific folders or tables inside a Fabric item and then assign those roles to users or groups. The permissions apply across all Fabric engines. Row-level and column-level security can narrow table access further, and a ReadWrite permission, available only for lakehouses, allows writing through Spark notebooks, the OneLake file explorer or OneLake APIs without rights to manage Fabric items. New items come with a DefaultReader role whose membership is virtualized, so anyone with the needed permission such as ReadAll is automatically a member. Because that role grants full access, users should be removed from it once they are placed in a more restrictive role. Creating roles requires write and reshare permission, usually held by workspace admins and members. For SQL analytics endpoints, the access mode must be switched to the user's identity mode, since new endpoints start in delegated identity mode and are not protected by OneLake security until then. Users without any data access role see no data in the item. The page lists lakehouses and mirrored items as supported and gives no license details.

onnx-runtime.title: ONNX Runtime and Models – Azure Machine Learning – Microsoft Learn
onnx-runtime.notes: ONNX Runtime is a high-performance inference engine for running ONNX models in production. Its purpose is to speed up inference, meaning scoring a deployed model on production data. The idea is that a model is trained once in a preferred framework, exported or converted to the ONNX format, and then runs in the cloud or at the edge. The engine is written in C++ and offers APIs for C, Python, C#, Java and JavaScript on Linux, Windows and macOS. It supports deep neural networks as well as classical machine learning models and can use accelerators such as TensorRT on NVIDIA GPUs, OpenVINO on Intel processors and DirectML on Windows. For Python, the packages onnxruntime and onnxruntime-gpu are installed from PyPI, and a session object loads the model file and runs it on input data. It is integrated into Windows Machine Learning, Azure SQL Edge, Azure SQL Managed Instance and ML.NET, and in Azure Machine Learning an ONNX model can be deployed as a REST endpoint through an MLOps workflow. The page reports an average CPU speedup in internal Microsoft services but stresses that gains depend on many factors, and not every model converts successfully.

openid-connect.title: OpenID Connect (OIDC) on the Microsoft identity platform – Microsoft Learn
openid-connect.notes: OpenID Connect extends the OAuth 2.0 authorization protocol with authentication, which makes single sign-on possible between OAuth-enabled applications. Identity is carried in a security token called the ID token, a JWT signed with public-key cryptography, from which a client can verify the user and read claims about them. The Microsoft identity platform exposes a discovery document on a well-known path, a key endpoint for signature verification, authorize and token endpoints, a logout endpoint and a UserInfo endpoint that returns claims based on the openid, profile and email scopes. An app needs a registration in Microsoft Entra ID, a matching registered redirect URI and ID token issuance enabled, and a sign-in request must include the client ID, the id_token response type, the openid scope and a nonce. Apps that use ID tokens must validate signature and claims, ideally with a token validation library. The page notes that native apps and single-page apps gain little from such validation, that sign-out needs both the end-session redirect and clearing the app session, and that fragment responses are limited in length, so form_post is recommended. Tokens issued for other Microsoft APIs should not be read or validated.

parameter-sniffing.title: Query processing architecture guide – SQL Server – Microsoft Learn
parameter-sniffing.notes: The guide covers parameter sniffing in a section on parameter sensitivity. In this process the database engine inspects the current parameter values while compiling or recompiling a query and hands them to the query optimizer, which can then produce more efficient execution plans. It applies to stored procedures, queries run through sp_executesql and prepared queries, and it interacts with plan reuse because compiled plans are stored in the plan cache. One described remedy is the OPTION (RECOMPILE) hint, under which the optimizer treats parameters and local variables as compile-time constants that can be folded into literals. The values used are those in effect right before the statement, which are not necessarily the originally passed ones, and this can help with highly variable or skewed input data. The page warns that this hint recompiles the query on every execution, which can be expensive, and advises measuring the effect on the whole workload first. Values of local variables are not sniffed at compile time. Instead the optimizer estimates from density information or, without statistics, uses fixed percentage guesses for equality and range comparisons. The page also points to the Parameter Sensitive Plan optimization article.

phi-4.title: Phi Open Models – Small Language Models – Microsoft Azure
phi-4.notes: Phi is the Microsoft family of small language models, designed so developers can run AI directly on a device without a cloud connection. According to the FAQ on the page, the models are open source under the MIT License. Phi-4 targets complex reasoning and mathematical problem solving. Phi-4-mini adds a large vocabulary, grouped-query attention, built-in function calling, better instruction following and shared embeddings compared with Phi-3.5-mini. Phi-4-multimodal handles text, audio and image input, supports more than 20 languages and covers tasks such as speech recognition, translation, summarization, audio understanding, OCR and chart or table analysis. Earlier series such as Phi-3.5, Phi-3, Phi-2, Phi-1.5 and Phi-1 are also listed. Described uses include low-latency applications, local operation with or without cloud access, cost-constrained tasks, fine-tuning on domain data and production deployments. The models are available through Azure AI Foundry Models, Hugging Face and Ollama, and through Azure as pay-as-you-go model-as-a-service over inference APIs. Phi was originally optimized mainly for English, and the public training data has a stated cutoff date. The page gives no hardware requirements.

power-platform-pipelines.title: Overview of pipelines in Power Platform – Microsoft Learn
power-platform-pipelines.notes: Pipelines in Power Platform are a built-in Microsoft feature for application lifecycle management and CI/CD automation across Power Platform and Dynamics 365. Administrators configure deployment pipelines through a central pipelines host environment, makers deploy solutions straight from their development environment, and developers can run pipelines with the Power Platform CLI. Linked environments are typed as development or target environments. Before a deployment it checks for missing dependencies and validates connections and variables. The same solution artifact moves through the stages in a fixed order without being exported again, approvals can be handled through delegated deployments, and managed and unmanaged solutions are backed up in the host at each deployment. An audit log and Power BI reports are included, and earlier solution versions can be redeployed when rollback is enabled. Developer-type development and test environments need no standalone license, other environments must be managed environments, and a production target needs licenses with premium rights. Limits include no Dataverse table data, one solution per deployment, no cross-tenant deployment, one development environment per solution and one host per environment.
